answer.rationale: Two problems are live: competitor pricing pressure on SMB and declining activation/onboarding completion. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitive threat, but the archived record explicitly warns it hurt 30-day retention and should not be generalized as a growth lever — pursuing it risks trading short-term acquisition for long-term qualified revenue, which conflicts with the stated objective. Simplify_onboarding is directly relevant to the observed 4% onboarding completion drop and has two independent supporting memories (31, 86) showing durable activation lift without noted downside, making it the lower-risk, more defensible use of the single experiment slot. I verify memory_73 to confirm the retention harm before ruling promotional pricing out despite competitive pressure, and memory_31 to confirm the causal onboarding-simplification result before committing this week's capacity to it. Activation messaging and referral incentives remain plausible alternatives but are secondary to the onboarding regression signal this quarter. Scale is kept small/guarded since this is a single test and we should avoid overcommitting before observing whether the onboarding fix also lifts activation.
